Team — quick initial triage:
- Nothing scheduled in control plane at 07:40; no deployments.
- Platform telemetry shows an increase in upstream 5xx errors from the auth gateway cluster located in us-west-2 around 07:42.
- Correlation: a subset of requests with expired or malformed JWTs are being routed to the token-validation path that returns 401, but a mis-handled error path in our proxy was mapping certain auth errors to 502/503/429 when the downstream token service timed out.

I attached a short debug dump from the gateway for the 07:42-07:55 window (debug-logs-20270614.txt). Initial mitigation I recommend: toggle the auth-gateway fallback to return 401/403 for auth failures and throttle proportional to explicit 429 signals from rate-limiter instead of the generic retry ramp.

I'll push a hotfix to the proxy error-mapping and open IFR-4521.

— Dev

Subject: Post-incident: Auth gateway error-mapping & client recommendations

Hi Liam — following up with the post-incident summary and actions we've completed: 

Incident summary:
- Impact window: 2027-06-14T07:42 to 2027-06-14T09:30 PDT. Elevated 5xx/429 counts were caused by a proxy error-mapping path that converted token-validation timeouts into 502/503/429 instead of surface 401/403. That classification caused some Greenleaf clients to aggressively retry and produce a retry storm.
- Root cause: a race condition in the proxy when token-validation returned an io-timeout; the error handler defaulted to gateway-retry semantics. Also observed a small subset of requests with clock-skewed JWTs that triggered validation failures.

Remediations completed:
- Hotfix deployed on 2027-06-14: correct error-mapping to return 401/403 for auth failures and preserve explicit 429 semantics from rate-limiter.
- Added a guard to detect likely clock-skewed tokens and return a clear error hint so clients can optionally resync time instead of retrying immediately.
- Alerting/observability updates: new metric (auth.error_classification) and dashboard (INF-4521) to detect auth->5xx regressions; sample logs retained for 72h and linked to your case.
- Client recommendations: implement exponential backoff with jitter, treat 4xx auth failures as non-retriable, and add client-side clock sync checks before token refresh (details in mitigation_runbook_v1.pdf).

If you want, we can schedule a short technical review next week to walk through the fix and add any account-specific guardrails. Thanks again for your patience and for sending clear telemetry that helped narrow scope.

— Soojin
Senior Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
